title: The Day of the Labelled Drawer
skyStory: The moon has moved into Virgo, fifty-seven percent lit and carrying a label maker. Virgo moons sort, tidy and alphabetise; they find crumbs in corners nobody knew existed. It is the last day of November, the dark is long and the first real snow is gossiping at the edge of the forecast. Virgo would like everything in its proper drawer before December walks in.

reading: One drawer in the cabin has become a legend: odd keys, old batteries, three mystery cables, a single chess piece. Today Virgo hands you a label maker, metaphorically, and asks you to sort it. Ten minutes. Not a whole room. One drawer.

As you sort, you will find something you thought was gone forever, probably small, probably silly, definitely delightful. Keep it on the desk as a trophy. The month started with one spark, one plan and a brand-new moon. It ends with an orderly drawer and a full heart. The [[Knight of Wands]] salutes you with a slightly smaller torch, which is progress.
joel.mission: Sort one drawer in ten minutes flat, timer on, and label it with a ridiculous official name.
joel.omen: A lost key turning up exactly where you already looked. Something you gave up on is ready to come back.

reading: December is knocking, and December is your month: the solstice, the light returning, your birthday glowing on the horizon like a lighthouse. Virgo sees it coming and wants to help you get the shore ready. Expect the tide to tidy the beach overnight, all by itself.

Make a short list, in your best handwriting, of three things you want to do for yourself before the solstice. Not for anyone else. Not to earn anything. Just three joys, written down where Saturn can see them. [[The Sun]] is warming up on the far side of the long dark, and it has already started counting down.
nancy.mission: Write three solstice wishes for yourself on a card and tuck it behind the mirror until December 22.
nancy.omen: Neatly stacked firewood or a perfectly folded towel. Order is a love letter, and someone is writing you one.
nancy.stoneWhy: your left wrist, steady and sure
nancy.elementWhy: solid ground for the turning year

together.text: Look back at the word you each picked on the tenth. Did November live up to it? Score it out of eleven. Then choose a word for December together, one word, shared, and write it somewhere you will both see it every day until the solstice.

game.intro: Last night of November. The drawers are labelled, the moon is half-lit, and the buzzer is twitchy. Go.
